s01-R.text: Open the engine and fix it, with oily hands and no one to ask for help
s01-R.note: 'open and fix' is one repair sequence

s01-I.text: Work out from tides and wind why it stalled, though the answer may come too late
s01-I.dominant_activity: diagnose the stall from tides and wind

s01-A.text: Paint a big board so the crowd knows what is happening, with an hour to finish
s01-A.note: purpose is informing the crowd; A still dominant via 'paint'

s01-S.text: Keep the waiting children calm and busy, even if you miss the repair
s01-S.note: 'calm and busy' are two states, one activity

s02-R.text: Fit the new planks by hand in the cold, getting every joint tight before midnight
s02-R.note: uses trigger phrases 'by hand' and 'every joint'; planks vs stone arch slightly off-setting

s02-I.text: Find out why this arch cracked, even if it takes all night of measuring
s02-I.dominant_activity: find the cause of the crack

s02-A.text: Sketch a new arch shape that might be safer, though most first ideas get thrown out
s02-A.note: 'might be safer' adds an engineering reading

s02-E.text: Take charge of the repair team and the money, and face the blame if it goes wrong
s02-E.dominant_activity: lead the repair team + control the money

s03-R.text: Climb the tower and follow the broken gear by hand, in a dusty, cramped space
s03-R.dominant_activity: trace the broken gear in the tower
s03-R.note: 'climb ... and follow' is travel + task; uses trigger 'by hand'

s03-I.text: Study the pattern of missed chimes, though it may take days to spot the cause
s03-I.dominant_activity: study the pattern of missed chimes

s03-A.text: Repaint the clock face so it is easier to read, even if some liked the old one
s03-A.note: legibility purpose is functional but painting dominates

s03-C.text: Plan the repair step by step and list the parts needed, rewriting it as things change
s03-C.note: two distinct C tasks (sequencing and inventory); 'plan the repair' can read as managing

s04-R.text: Run the press and keep it humming all day
s04-R.note: no cost clause (whole stop lacks them)

s04-I.text: Test apple blends to find which one tastes best

s04-S.text: Teach visiting children to make juice through games
s04-S.note: 'through games' adds fun; uses trigger 'teach ... children'; no cost clause

s04-E.text: Persuade passers-by to buy and strike a good deal
s04-E.note: persuading and bargaining are two skills

s05-R.text: Mend the dim signal lamp alone on the ridge, in freezing wind

s05-I.text: Map where the fog is thickest to find a safer path, standing still in the cold
s05-I.dominant_activity: map fog density to find a path

s05-S.text: Gather the lost travellers and keep their spirits up on a long, cold walk
s05-S.note: 'gather' reads as rounding up/leading; 'keep spirits up' is the S part

s05-C.text: Count everyone through the pass so no one is left behind, even as people grow impatient
s05-C.note: 'so no one is left behind' has a caring tone

s06-R.text: Build a sturdy stall frame from the plan, working fast as the light fades

s06-I.text: Examine the old machine to learn its use, though it may turn out to be junk

s06-E.text: Set prices and win over buyers, knowing some will walk away

s06-C.text: Sort the stock and label shelves so buyers find things fast, before the doors open
s06-C.note: two C tasks; also stall is described as empty

s07-R.text: Build a raft from whatever wood is nearby, with sore arms and wet feet

s07-A.text: Draw up a boat for the crossing that may not float the first time
s07-A.note: 'draw up a boat ... may not float' reads as engineering; A cue is weak

s07-S.text: Care for the tired travellers through the night while others plan the crossing

s07-E.text: Run the camp meeting and push for a decision, even if some people are unhappy
s07-E.dominant_activity: run the meeting toward a decision
s07-E.note: 'run and push' is one leadership act

s08-R.text: Repair the creaking loom, crawling under it with tools for hours

s08-A.text: Design a banner pattern for the town, knowing not everyone will like it

s08-S.text: Coach a nervous new weaver, even though progress is slow and they may give up

s08-C.text: Track the cloth rolls for market day, recounting whenever the totals don't match

s09-R.text: Rope down a short stretch to test the rock, which is slow, tiring work
s09-R.dominant_activity: rope down to test the rock

s09-A.text: Draw a picture map of the glowing cliff for the climbers, redrawing it as the light shifts
s09-A.note: map is functional, but 'picture' and redrawing in shifting light keep it A

s09-E.text: Split the climbers into teams and set the pace, though some will grumble at your choices
s09-E.note: organising groups and directing pace are two acts

s09-C.text: Check every harness against the safety list while others start climbing first

s10-R.text: Haul the salt sacks off the road and stack them, heavy work in the heat

s10-S.text: Calm the gathering crowd and listen to each person's worry, which takes a while
s10-S.note: listening is the means of calming

s10-E.text: Settle the argument with a deal both traders accept, though neither is fully happy
s10-E.note: mediation can read as helping (S); 'deal' keeps E dominant

s10-C.text: Weigh what salt is left so each trader's loss is clear, with the crowd shouting nearby

s11-I.text: Chart the stars and wonder what is out there
s11-I.note: 'wonder' is evocative; no cost clause (whole stop)

s11-A.text: Paint the night sky and notice how it changes
s11-A.note: 'notice how it changes' is evocative; no cost clause

s11-S.text: Welcome the visitors and help each one find a good spot to look
s11-S.note: welcome + help is one hosting act

s11-E.text: Run the club night and sign up new members

s12-I.text: Test soils and seeds to grow healthier plants
s12-I.note: two objects, one activity; no cost clause (whole stop)

s12-A.text: Shape the garden so it feels peaceful to walk in

s12-S.text: Show children how to care for the plants through stories

s12-C.text: Label every herb and keep the beds in tidy rows
s12-C.dominant_activity: label herbs + keep beds in rows

s13-I.text: Investigate how the old press works, reading faded notes that may lead nowhere

s13-A.text: Design a new letter style for the press, then redo it if people can't read it

s13-E.text: Start a new newspaper and find people to pay for it, at the risk it does not sell

s13-C.text: Proofread each page before printing, starting over whenever a mistake slips through

s14-I.text: Test the water to find what is making people ill, with many tests that show nothing
s14-I.dominant_activity: test the water for the cause of illness

s14-S.text: Sit with the sick travellers and talk with them, though some would rather be left alone
s14-S.dominant_activity: sit and talk with the sick
s14-S.note: sit with + talk is one act of companionship

s14-E.text: Lead the clinic team and choose who is seen first, even when someone has to wait
s14-E.dominant_activity: lead the team + decide triage order
s14-E.note: leading and prioritising patients are two acts

s14-C.text: Sort the medicine store so the right dose is quick to find, checking label after label

s15-A.text: Create the welcome arch, though you may still be painting it as the lamps arrive

s15-S.text: Greet newcomers and help them join in, staying by the gate while the fun starts
s15-S.note: greet + help join is one welcoming act

s15-E.text: Run the stalls and set the prices, then face the stallholders if sales are slow

s15-C.text: Keep the timetable so every act starts on time, working out of sight all evening
